summary: A is preferable because its replayable-body implementation is safer and its tests better cover the frozen contract, although both patches need revision before merge because Upload bypasses FilesService.Add and both expand retry machinery beyond the requested scope.
reasons: Both implementations violate the explicit requirement to route Upload through FilesService.Add; each duplicates option handling, request construction, response decoding, and the missing-data error.
A tests source-reader failure propagation and FilesOption forwarding, while B omits the contract-required source-reader error test.
A's buffered bytes.Reader provides stable replay semantics. B's GetBody returns wrappers around the same mutable io.ReadSeeker, so bodies are not independent as GetBody conventionally promises.
B's wireSeekableRequestBody can leave the source positioned at EOF if seeking to the end succeeds but restoring the original offset fails, causing the initial request to send incorrect content.
risks_a: RawClient.Do now buffers nearly every reader unless WithNoRetry is set, creating broad memory, streaming, read-timing, and reader-ownership changes outside the requested Upload API.
The RawClient changes and associated README/changelog claims conflict with the contract's scope restriction against unrelated retry refactoring.
Upload duplicates FilesService.Add instead of reusing it.
risks_b: Upload duplicates FilesService.Add instead of reusing it.
The required source-reader error behavior is implemented indirectly but not tested.

The bespoke seekableBody changes caller-reader closing semantics and Content-Length behavior across RawClient users, expanding API behavior beyond scope of the upload convenience method and increasing maintenance risk.
